Title: Diagnosis of test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord`

Details: The test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord` aims to verify that an `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown when trying to access the CSV record with an inconsistent header mapping (in this case, adding a new header "fourth" and then calling `recordWithHeader.get("fourth")`).

The relevant method involved is `CSVRecord.get(String name)`:
- It first checks if the `mapping` (header to index map) is null, and if so, throws an `IllegalStateException`.
- Then, it gets the index for the given header name from the `mapping`.
- If the index is not found in `mapping` (index is null), it returns null.
- If the index is found, it returns the corresponding value from the `values` array using this index.

The test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` when accessing a non-existing header ("fourth"). However, the current implementation of `CSVRecord.get(String name)` doesn't throw any `IllegalArgumentException` if the header name does not exist in `mapping` – it simply returns null. This behavior is inconsistent with the test expectation that an exception should be thrown for an unknown header key.

Hence, the bug occurs because the `CSVRecord.get(String name)` method does not throw an `IllegalArgumentException` when the requested header name is not present in the `mapping`. This leads to the test failure because the exception expected by the test never occurs.

The proper fix is likely to involve modifying `CSVRecord.get(String name)` so that it throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if the header name is not found in the mapping, instead of returning null.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.get(java.lang.String)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
